description: Bug backlog. Process: docs/issues.md. Sibling of feature_list.json; the leader appends new reports as 'reported'.

rules.one_in_progress_across_both_lists: no feature and issue in_progress at the same time. Among issues there is no cap: a whole approved batch may sit in_progress together, implemented by one implementer run and reviewed by one batched reviewer call (owner directive 2026-09-22). reviewed: true marks an issue the reviewer APPROVED; status stays in_progress until the human marks it done.
rules.human_only_transitions: pending -> approved | wontfix, and -> done. Agents never make these.

fields.name: kebab-case slug; folder is issues/<name>/
fields.title: one line
fields.severity: low | medium | high | critical, as reported (triager may amend in analysis.md)
fields.covers: FR-*/NFR-* ids the defect violates; filled by issue_triager
fields.classification: defect | spec_gap | arch_pending | not_a_defect; filled by issue_triager
fields.reviewed: bool, set by the leader (targeted edit) after a reviewer APPROVED verdict; owner directive 2026-09-22, see docs/issues.md

issues.name: login-timing-username-enumeration
issues.title: Login skips the password hash when the account does not exist, so response time reveals which usernames exist
issues.report: From the 2026-11-02 auth architecture review: login() returns early without running PBKDF2 when the account is missing (OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet: run the hash regardless of whether the user exists). Fix: verify against a dummy hash for an unknown username so both paths cost one PBKDF2. Touches planner_core (application/authentication.py).

issues.name: authorizer-builds-full-dependency-graph
issues.title: The authorizer Lambda builds the whole dependency graph (SQS, every repository) when it only needs accounts, signer and clock
issues.report: From the 2026-11-02 auth architecture review: planner_api authorizer calls build_dependencies(), which wires everything and needs GENERATION_QUEUE_URL, lengthening the serial cold start (authorizer then api). Fix: build only accounts, signer and clock for the authorizer, and drop GENERATION_QUEUE_URL from the authorizer's environment in terraform/locals.tf (terraform edit is done separately by the Terraform agent after approval).

issues.name: lambda-handler-receives-context-as-deps
issues.title: Every deployed Lambda entry point treats the Lambda context as its injected dependencies, so no deployed route works
issues.report: Login on the deployed dev app returns the generic 'Se ha producido un error inesperado'. CloudWatch (api Lambda, 2026-11-04T22:09:32Z): handler.py line 90 handle -> routing.py line 122 _login accounts=deps.accounts -> AttributeError: 'LambdaContext' object has no attribute 'accounts'. Cause seen by the leader: lambda_handler = handle, AWS calls handle(event, context), so the context lands in the deps parameter and `deps or build_dependencies()` keeps it. The same shape exists in authorizer.py, scheduled.py and planner_ai/handler.py. Owner asked for a deeper triage and a better-thought solution than a one-line wrapper.

issues.name: ai-kill-switch-unreadable-under-shared-role
issues.title: AI generation is always off in the deployed app: the shared Lambda role cannot read the SSM kill switch
issues.report: Owner, 2026-11-06: "I can't ask for it. So, for the future when this app runs in my own environment I control I will use SSM, because it aligns better, but for now let's just use Lambda env var to work around. I will explain in the docs". CloudWatch (ai Lambda, 2026-11-06T19:47:52Z): SSM switch /planner/dev/ai-generation-enabled unreadable (AccessDeniedException AccessDeniedException); generation fails closed. studentLambdaExecutionRole has no ssm:GetParameter and the owner can neither edit the role nor have it edited.

issues.name: deployed-lambdas-drop-info-logs
issues.title: Deployed Lambdas send no INFO log lines to CloudWatch, so successful requests leave no application log
issues.report: From triaging issue 23, confirmed against invocations the owner pasted: 9882e790 (ai) shows START, [WARNING], END with no 'Processed ...' line, and 4f4e8a98 (api) shows START, [ERROR], END with no 'Handled request' line, which handler.py:104 logs in a finally. Nothing raises the level: basicConfig runs only in the local entry points and terraform/ has no logging_config, and AWS documents WARN as the plain-text default for Python runtimes. specs/rest_api_lambda R22 (NFR-OBS-01) requires one record per invocation. Owner, 2026-11-07: 'propose an approach for this, I would also enable debug level on dev env'. Tested locally with fake values: at root DEBUG, botocore writes the GetSecretValue session key, a DynamoDB passHash and the Bedrock bearer token to the log; setting the boto3, botocore, urllib3 and s3transfer loggers to WARNING stops all three and keeps app DEBUG lines. The backend has no logger.debug calls today. Owner rulings, 2026-11-07, on the leader's proposal: approach OK (JSON log format and a level per environment in Terraform, DEBUG on dev and INFO elsewhere; SDK loggers set to WARNING in code from each Lambda entry point; root level not set in code; the local fake-secret check becomes a regression test). No debug lines added now. The leader adds the Terraform once the fix is approved.

issues.name: ai-failed-messages-never-retried
issues.title: Suspected: failed AI queue messages are never retried and never reach the dead-letter queue
issues.report: Suspected from reading the code, not observed on AWS. terraform/lambda.tf sets function_response_types = ["ReportBatchItemFailures"] on the ai queue mapping, but planner_ai/handler.py handle() catches every exception per record, logs it and returns None, and lambda_handler returns None too. If the empty response counts as success, a failed message is deleted, so there is no retry and the generation_dlq alarm in terraform/monitoring.tf cannot fire for it. The catch is commented as per-record isolation (R4), so whether this is intended needs checking. Owner, 2026-11-07: 'log but do not start triaging or doing anything with them yet'.

issues.name: if-none-match-exact-case-lookup
issues.title: Suspected: the conditional GET looks up If-None-Match by exact case, so a lower-case header would never match
issues.report: Suspected from reading the code, not observed on AWS. planner_api/handler.py:84 reads headers.get("If-None-Match") with exact case. local_server.py:65-69 normalises case locally and says a real API Gateway proxy event does not need it, which has not been checked. If the header arrives lower-case on the deployed path, the conditional GET never short-circuits. The Cookie lookup has the same shape but was seen working on dev, so that half is fine. Owner, 2026-11-07: 'log but do not start triaging or doing anything with them yet'.

issues.name: boto3-client-built-per-call
issues.title: Suspected: AWS SDK clients are rebuilt on each use instead of being reused across calls
issues.report: Suspected from reading the code, not measured. boto3.client or boto3.resource is called inside helper functions rather than held for reuse: adapters/ssm.py:37 and adapters/bedrock.py:154 in planner_ai, adapters/sqs.py:174 and adapters/secrets.py:18 in planner_api, and adapters/dynamo/_table.py in both packages. How often each runs per invocation, and what it costs, has not been checked. Owner, 2026-11-07: 'log but do not start triaging or doing anything with them yet'.
